newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-SAMPRAS SHOWS HIS HEART AT U.S. OPEN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SAMPRAS SHOWS HIS HEART AT U.S. OPEN.

text.p: Pete Sampras's enormous talent has long been obvious, but his U.S. Open performance this week has laid to rest any questions about his heart and desire.
Sampras feels that his sometimes listless appearance on the court has given people the impression that he doesn't care as much as some of his more animated rivals.
But the top-ranked player in the world feels that he has now proven his critics could not be more wrong.
"Throughout the past six months to a year, I have battled through some tough moments on and off the court," he said alluding to the death of his coach and friend Tim Gullikson.
"I think people see that I do care and I do want to win and I do have heart."

That became painfully obvious as he staggered like a punch-drunk fighter during the final points of his five-set tie-break win over Spaniard Alex Corretja in the quarter-finals in a courageous display of willpower.
"I was done. If it was a boxing match, I think the ref would have called it," said Sampras. "I just felt like I didn't want to give up."
On Saturday, Sampras returned after a day's rest to beat fourth-seeded Goran Ivanisevic 6-3 6-4 6-7 6-3 and reach the final against second-seeded countryman Michael Chang.
The seeds of Sampras's refuse-to-lose attitude were sewn four years ago when he lost to Stefan Edberg in the Open final.
"That really hurt me," said Sampras. "People don't remember who comes in second and that match woke me up to (the fact) that I really, really hate to lose.
"I learned over the years that I hate to lose and I will do whatever I can to win. If it's ugly, it's ugly, just as long as I win the last point."
Sunday's final will give Sampras his last chance to extend his streak of winning at least one Slam a year since 1993. Sampras promised to give it his all, as usual.
"I always measure my year by these (major) tournaments," he said. "It's crunch time. I have got to use every ounce of energy I have and go out and play."
